title: You can see where a dragged picture will land before you let go
goal: While you drag a capture over the canvas, nothing tells you where it will land or how big it will be, so the size is a surprise. Draw the box it would fill under the pointer while the drag is in the air, the way a component dragged off the shelf already does.
notes: The placement rule is PhotonzDocument.placementForIncomingImage (Sources/PhotonzCore/Clipboard.swift), so the preview and the drop can share one call. CanvasView already has the machinery for a component drag: componentLanding + trackComponentDrag + refreshOverlays (Sources/Photonz/CanvasView.swift ~1129). The missing piece is the image size during draggingUpdated: read it off the file URL with CGImageSourceCopyPropertiesAtIndex (kCGImagePropertyPixelWidth/Height), no decode needed, cached per draggingSequenceNumber. Found while auditing the drop-placement task on 2026-09-03; the hold shot Scripts/playtest/drop-lands-here-walk.json takes (1-tile-in-the-air) shows the empty canvas this would fill.
acceptance: Dragging a capture over the canvas draws an outline of exactly the box it would land in
The outline follows the pointer, and snaps to the screen under the pointer when there is one
The outline disappears the moment the drag leaves the canvas or is let go
A scripted walk photographs the outline while the drag is still in the air
